newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds fall in "logical" profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds fall in "logical" profit-taking.

text.p: Argentine bonds were lower late morning Wednesday as investors decided to book some profits after the recent run up.
"This is a logical decline" after the recent gains, said a trader at a foreign bank. The market had risen for six consecutive sessions.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 fell 3/8 to 92-6/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was $0.55 lower at 115.20.
Apart from the desire of some investors to take profits, another trader said declines in U.S. Treasuries were also weighing on the market in the morning.

Traders said a small market shake-out could be welcome news as some investors, particularly overseas funds, had not taken part in the recent rally. This decline could give them the opportunity to take out new positions, thus fuelling more gains in the medium-term.
